Recent papers on Multi-Modal Models. ## Foundations ### What are Multi-Modal Models? Multi-modal models process and reason across multiple types of data — text, images, audio, video, and structured data — within a single system. Unlike unimodal models that handle one input type, multi-modal systems can draw inferences across modalities, enabling capabilities like visual question answering, image captioning, audio understanding, and cross-modal reasoning. ### Core Architectures ```{mermaid} graph TB subgraph VLM["Vision-Language Model"] I[Image] --> VE[Visual Encoder
ViT/SigLIP] T[Text] --> TE[Text Encoder
LLM] VE --> Proj[Projection Layer] Proj --> LLM[Language Model] TE --> LLM LLM --> O[Output: Caption, Answer, etc.] end subgraph Audio["Audio-Language Model"] A[Audio] --> AE[Audio Encoder] AE --> LLM2[Language Model] LLM2 --> O2[Output] end subgraph Omni["Omni-Modal Model"] I2[Image] --> Shared[Shared Encoder] A2[Audio] --> Shared T2[Text] --> Shared Shared --> LLM3[Language Model] LLM3 --> O3[Output] end ``` - **Vision-Language Models (VLMs)**: Combine a visual encoder (e.g., ViT, SigLIP) with a language model, projecting image features into the same embedding space as text. Examples: LLaVA, GPT-4V, Gemini, Qwen-VL. - **Audio-Language Models**: Integrate speech recognition and audio understanding with language models for tasks like spoken dialogue, audio captioning, and sound event detection. - **Omni-Modal Models**: Unified architectures that handle text, images, audio, and video in a single model with shared representations. ### Key Capabilities 1. **Visual Question Answering**: Answering questions about images using both visual and linguistic understanding 2. **Image/Video Captioning**: Generating natural language descriptions of visual content 3. **Document Understanding**: Reading and reasoning about scanned documents, charts, tables, and screenshots 4. **Grounded Generation**: Producing outputs tied to specific regions of an image or moments in a video 5. **Cross-Modal Reasoning**: Using information from one modality to inform understanding of another ### Training Approaches - **Contrastive Learning**: Aligning representations across modalities (e.g., CLIP matches images to text descriptions) - **Instruction Tuning**: Fine-tuning on multi-modal instruction datasets for task following - **Mixture-of-Experts (MoE)**: Using specialized expert sub-networks for different modalities or tasks, enabling efficient scaling - **Continual Learning**: Sequentially acquiring new multi-modal capabilities without forgetting previously learned ones ### Key Challenges - **Catastrophic forgetting**: Learning new modalities or tasks can degrade performance on old ones - **Hallucination**: Models may generate plausible but incorrect descriptions of visual content - **Safety**: Multi-modal inputs create new attack surfaces — adversarial images, misleading documents, harmful audio - **Evaluation**: Benchmarks must test genuine cross-modal reasoning, not just unimodal shortcuts ## Active Research Directions ### Multimodal Safety Moderation (Week 35) Nemotron 3.5 demonstrates compact multimodal content safety moderation across images, documents, screenshots, and text under domain-varying policies. Moving beyond text-only guardrails to comprehensive multimodal safety. ### Continual Multimodal Learning (Week 35) CoRe-MoE addresses catastrophic forgetting in multimodal instruction tuning through compact, reusable Mixture-of-Experts with LoRA. Enables sequential task acquisition while preserving previously learned knowledge. ### Multimodal Search Agents (Week 35) WeAgent-MMSearch enables native text-vision interaction for multimodal search, ensuring retrieved images remain in context for visually grounded trajectories rather than being discarded as text-only. ### Accessibility Planning (Week 35) MAP benchmark evaluates multimodal AI as assistants for users with accessibility requirements, verifying or recommending points of interest meeting specific accessibility needs. ## Key Concepts - **Multimodal Safety**: Content moderation across images, documents, screenshots under varying policies - **Continual Multimodal Learning**: Sequential task acquisition without catastrophic forgetting - **Native Text-Vision Interaction**: Keeping retrieved images in context for grounded reasoning - **Accessibility-Aware Planning**: Multimodal systems assisting users with specific accessibility requirements - **Compact Safety Models**: Small multimodal models for deployment-time safety moderation ## Recent Papers ### [2608.27548] Nemotron 3.5 Content Safety Moderator: A Compact Multimodal, Multilingual, and Reasoning Enabled Content Safety Moderator - **Authors:** Singh, V, Doshi, A, Narsimhan, M, Ghosh, S, Luna, K - **Date:** 2026-08-31 - **URL:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27548 - **Abstract:** Safety moderation for deployed AI applications is moving beyond text-only prompts: systems increasingly need to judge images, documents, screenshots, and generated responses under policies that vary across domains.
